## Description

**What**: Update existing project documentation to reflect the new _phase_remediate phase, lib/ci-findings-normalize.sh, per-tier bounding, escalation JSON contract, exit code 2 semantics, and any new config keys introduced by the epic.

**Why**: Ensures future agents and developers have accurate awareness of the remediation phase, its contract, and its consumer impact — preventing configuration drift and misuse of the escalation payload.

**Scope**:
- IN: CLAUDE.md quick reference (update merge-to-main phases section); CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md (new config keys if any, e.g., review.max_remediation_attempts); merge-to-main-pr.sh inline docs (phase summary, exit codes); merge-to-main.sh dispatcher inline docs (exit code 2 semantics for remediation exhaustion); sprint SKILL.md (note escalation JSON contract and exit code 2 handling); COMMIT-WORKFLOW.md (note escalation JSON contract); KNOWN-ISSUES.md (if applicable)
- OUT: New documentation files; documentation for story-level implementation details

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, CLAUDE.md and CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md accurately describe the _phase_remediate phase, any new config keys, and the exit code semantics (exit 1 = pre-remediation failure, exit 2 = remediation exhaustion)
  ← Satisfies: "SC5: runs end-to-end in a sprint session" (documentation prerequisite for sprint agents)
- When this story is complete, merge-to-main.sh dispatcher inline docs, sprint SKILL.md, and COMMIT-WORKFLOW.md reference the exit code 2 semantics and escalation JSON contract location so consumers handle remediation exhaustion correctly rather than treating it as a generic non-zero exit
  ← Satisfies: "SC4: structured JSON escalation payload" (consumer-facing documentation)

## Considerations

- Follow .claude/docs/DOCUMENTATION-GUIDE.md for documentation formatting, structure, and conventions
- Only update existing docs — do not create new documentation files
- Verify all OUT assertions: CLAUDE.md already exists (Verified: file present); COMMIT-WORKFLOW.md already exists (check path); sprint SKILL.md path to verify

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: Update project docs to reflect PR merge remediation loop
